record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.context_brief: Plane maps conjugate to complex polynomials
record.original_question: Characterize the self-mappings of the plane that are conjugate to a complex polynomial, separately in the three senses listed by Targonski: conjugacy under a diffeomorphism, under a homeomorphism, and under an arbitrary bijection.

evidence.quote: However, we would like to remaind the following problem posed by Gy. Targonski [248]: Characterize all self-mappings of the plane which are conjugated to a complex polynomial (a) under a diffeomorphism, (b) under a homeomorphism, (c) under a bijection.

artifact.category_tag: Iteration theory and conjugacy of plane maps
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question by Gy. Targonski in iteration theory, and surveys of recent progress on functional equations in a single variable continue to list it among open problems. No characterization in any of the three senses (diffeomorphism, homeomorphism, arbitrary bijection) appears to have been established in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing Targonski's problem of characterizing self-mappings of the plane conjugate to a complex polynomial under (a) a diffeomorphism, (b) a homeomorphism, (c) a bijection.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is presented as an open question of Targonski in a recent survey on functional equations in a single variable.
